monument_name: Gaṇeśa Mandira (reconstructed in 2000 CE in its present look)
description_en: Gaṇeśa Mandira is located at the Sāymi Ṭola, Kirtipur. This place is mostly inhabited by the members of the Mānandhara caste. A family from this caste runs aguṭhīassociated with the temple, sponsorsing for the display of a metal statue of Gaṇeśa in the temple every year on the full moon day of Śrāvaṇa (also called Guṃlāpunhī), on the Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī and Indra Jātrā Day. Theguṭhīhas no regular income in the present-day. The residents of Ṭola worship this Gaṇeśa before they start any auspicious occasions such as initiation, marriage, birthday and alike.There is no evidence to date the initial construction of the temple. It was jointly reconstructed in its present-day shape by the Department of Archaeology and local residents in around 2000 CE.The temple was in ruins until 1970s and was then reconstructed in a rectangular shape using modern bricks and cement (see a picture of the temple taken around that time which is published inShokoohy and others2014, 176). Even though reconstructed in concrete, the temple’s old wooden elements such as windows,toraṇa,and alike were reused wherever possible. It was demolished in the late 1990s and reconstructed in its present-day shape.There is a stoneśikhara-styled shrine inside the temple’s sanctum. An aniconic stone, worshipped as Gaṇeśa, is placed in the middle of the shrine and crowned by a stonetoraṇa. This shrine probably constitutes the preceding structure of this temple and the contemporary structure was probably constructed around this stone shrine. Such examples are not rare in Patan. The Gaṇeśa Temples in Mikhā Bāhāḥ (LAL0820) and in Jena Bāhāḥ (LAL0270) also have the similar structures.
description_ne: यो गणेश मन्दिर साय्मि टोलमा अवस्थित छ । साय्‌मि टोल मानन्धर समुदायको वाहुल्यता भएको टोल हो । सोही समुदायको एक खलकले यस गणेशको गुठी संचालन गर्दै आएको छ । गुठीले गुंलापुन्ही (श्रावण शुक्ल पूर्णिमा), कृष्णाष्टमी र इन्द्रजात्रामा यस मन्दिरमा धातुको गणेश मूर्ति प्रदर्शनमा राख्ने परम्परा चलाउँदै आएको छ । उक्त गुठीमा हाल कुनै पनि नियमित आयस्ताको व्यवस्था छैन ।साय्मि टोलका मानन्धर र अन्य समुदायले कुनै पनि शुभकार्य पूर्व यस गणेशलाई विशेष पूजा अपर्ण गर्दै आएको छ ।यहाँ मन्दिरको प्ररम्भिक निर्माणबारे उल्लेख परेको कुनैपनि अभिलेख प्राप्त छैन । मन्दिरको  हालको स्वरूपमा पुनःनिर्माण गर्ने कार्य सन् २००० को दशकमा पुरातत्व विभाग र स्थानीयको सहभागितामा भएको हो । सन् १९७० को दशकतिर भत्की विग्री बसेको गणेश मन्दिरलाई आधुनिक इँट र सिमेण्टको प्रयोग गरी एक तले वर्गाकार भवनको संरचनामा निर्माण गरिएको थियो । उक्त संरचनामा निर्मित यस मन्दिरको पूर्वरूपShokoohy and others(2014,176) द्वारा प्रकाशित फोटोमा देख्न सकिन्छ । क्रंक्रिडको भवन भए तापनि पुराना अवशेषका रूपमा बचेका झ्याल, तोरण, सिंह आदिलाई उक्त भवनमा पुनः प्रयोगमा ल्याइएको थियो ।यो भवन पनि सन् १९९० को अन्ततिर भत्किए पश्चात् मन्दिरलाई हालको स्वरूपमा बनाइएको हो । मन्दिरको गर्भगृहमा ढुङ्गाबाट निर्मित गजूर सहितको शिखराकार shrine छ । उक्त shrine को मध्य भागमा ढुङ्गाकै तोरण सिहतको खोपो छ जसभित्र गणेश मानी पूजिने अमूर्त ढुङ्गा छ । ढुङ्गाबाट बनेको यस शिखराकार shrine यहाँको प्रारम्भिक संरचना हो । उक्त shrine लाई बीचमा पारी पछि मात्र मन्दिर उठाइएको देखिन्छ ।यसरी पहिलै भएको ढुङ्गाको shrine वा मन्दिरलाई केन्द्रमा पारी त्यसमाथि तल्ले शैलीका मन्दिर निर्माण गरिएको उदाहरणहरू पाटनमा पनि पाइन्छन् । पाटनको मिखाबाहाः स्थित गयणेश मन्दिर (LAL0820) र जेन बाहाः टोलको गणेश मन्दिरको (LAL0270) गर्भगृहमा पनि यहाँकै समान ढुङ्गाका शिखराकार shrine रहेका छन् ।
brick_type: dāci apā (conical veneer brick), mā apā (regular fired brick)

historical_events.event_description: The bell, established on the southeast corner of the temple with a cement pillar, was offered by a local Mānandhara family.

The temple had become dilapidated and was replaced around the 1970s with a small modern rectangular building with a cement slab. By the late 1990s, the concrete building had also fallen into disrepair and was eventually demolished.

In the beginning of the 2000s, the rebuilding of the temple in its original form was carried out in consultation with the Department of Archaeology (DoA). The DoA covered half of the expenses and the other half was raised from the local residents, who also provided free labour.
